claim: Arles' Roman and Romanesque monuments are inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1981), with the city second only to Rome in number of Roman remains preserved.
quote: Arles is a good example of the adaptation of an ancient city to medieval European civilization. It has some impressive Roman monuments, of which the earliest – the arena, the Roman theatre and the cryptoporticus (subterranean galleries) – date back to the 1st century B.C.

claim: The Arles Amphitheatre (Arènes) was built around 90 AD, seats up to 21,000, and in 2026 opens daily 9am–7pm (May–Sept) with €11 adult admission.
quote: Opening hours for 2026: May 1 to September 30 daily between 9 am and 7 pm; October 1-31 daily between 9 am and 6 pm; November 2 2026 to February 28 2027 daily between 10:30 am and 4:30 pm. Admission: €11 full price, €9 reduced.

claim: Frank Gehry's LUMA Arles Tower, panoramic terraces, Carsten Höller slides and the landscaped park/skatepark are free to access; only the exhibition galleries require a paid ticket, and admission is exceptionally free 1–30 April 2026.
quote: From April 1 to April 30, 2026, admission to LUMA Arles is exceptionally free and no ticket is required... The entrance to The Tower designed by Frank Gehry, the panoramic terraces, the slides created by artist Carsten Höller, as well as all artistic installations within The Tower are freely accessible.

claim: The Pass Liberté (€13–€15 adult, valid 1 month) bundles 4 monuments of choice (Amphitheatre, Théâtre Antique, Cloître Saint-Trophime, Cryptoportiques, Alyscamps, Thermes de Constantin) plus Musée Réattu and one more museum (Museon Arlaten / MDAA / Camargue), with a reduced rate at the Fondation Van Gogh.
quote: The Pass Liberté is valid for 1 month and gives you access to a choice of 4 monuments... + the Musée Réattu + a second museum of your choice... This pass also entitles you to a reduced rate for visits to the Vincent van Gogh Foundation in Arles.

claim: Fondation Vincent van Gogh Arles reopens 22 May 2026 with 'SUSPECTS — Van Gogh, Tricksters & Co.', running 22 May–18 October 2026, daily 10am–6pm (closed 27 April–21 May for changeover).
quote: SUSPECTS — VAN GOGH, TRICKSTERS & CO. ... The Foundation is closed from April 27 to May 21. We will reopen on Friday 22 May with an exhibition devoted to artists who, following Vincent van Gogh, have chosen dissidence over conformity and excess over restraint.

claim: Arles' Saturday open-air market runs along Boulevards des Lices and Clémenceau, 08:00–12:45, with roughly 450 vendors across about two kilometres — one of the largest in Provence.
quote: Open Air Market every Saturday morning on the Boulevards des Lices and Clémenceau in Arles... Saturday from 08:00 to 12:45.

claim: The Musée Départemental Arles Antique ('le musée bleu') displays the Arles-Rhône 3 — a 31-metre 1st-century Gallo-Roman flat-bottomed barge raised from the Rhône in 2011 — alongside major mosaics and the Arles bust of Julius Caesar.
quote: The Arles-Rhône 3 boat, a Gallo-Roman flat-bottomed barge raised from the Rhône in 2011, is the centerpiece of the permanent collection alongside mosaics, sculptures and the famous bust of Julius Caesar.

claim: Les Alyscamps is a Roman necropolis used for nearly 1,500 years; Van Gogh and Gauguin painted there side-by-side in late October 1888 (Van Gogh producing four canvases, Gauguin two).
quote: Vincent van Gogh and Paul Gauguin both painted The Alyscamps in 1888... van Gogh painted four canvases and Gauguin two during the period when they worked together at Arles.

claim: Espace Van Gogh — the former 16th-century Hôtel-Dieu where Van Gogh was treated after the December 1888 ear incident — has its courtyard garden restored to match his painting 'Le Jardin de la Maison de Santé'; entry is free.
quote: The 'Espace Van Gogh' is the former Hôtel-Dieu hospital where Van Gogh was treated after his ear-cutting episode. The inner garden has been faithfully restored to match the painting Vincent did of it... Free admission.

claim: Les Rencontres d'Arles 2026 — the world's largest photography festival — runs 6 July to 4 October 2026, with Opening Week 6–12 July taking over heritage sites across the city.
quote: Les Rencontres d'Arles 2026... from July 6 to October 4, 2026. Opening Week from July 6 to 12, 2026.

claim: The Théâtre Antique d'Arles, built around 12 BC under Augustus, originally seated ~10,000 and today retains two surviving columns of its scenae frons; admission €9 adult, open daily 9am–7pm in summer.
quote: Constructed during the reign of Emperor Augustus around 12 BCE... originally accommodated approximately 10,000 spectators... Standard adult tickets are around €9, with reduced rates.

claim: For day-trippers the best parking is the 500-space covered Parking du Centre (rue Émile Fassin, 24/7) or Parking des Lices; Parking Lamartine is closest to the Old Town but often full on Saturday market days.
quote: When visiting the historic center, it is best to park in the Parking des Lices or Parc du Centre, a covered car park with 500 spaces, accessible from rue Emile Fassin... Lamartine parking lot right by the northern entrance to the Old Town, though it's often full on busy market days.

claim: The Cryptoportiques are a 1st-century BC U-shaped underground Roman gallery that served as the foundation of the forum; entry €5, open 9am–7pm May–September.
quote: Built in the 1st century BC, these subterranean galleries served as the foundations of the Roman forum of Arles. The U-shaped gallery extends about 90 metres. Open 9am to 7pm May to September, admission €5.
